churn_resistance.rationale: Upgrading the framework would touch almost nothing, and data access is properly walled off; the friction lives in duplicated API type definitions, copy-pasted hydration plumbing, and missing error reporting that a future maintainer will have to retrofit.

findings.issue: Errors are logged only in import.meta.env.DEV and there is no handleError export in a revealed entry.server.tsx or onError on HydratedRouter, so production failures are silent
findings.suggestion: Follow RR 8.5's error-reporting doc: reveal the entries and add handleError (checking request.signal.aborted) plus a client onError hook

findings.issue: One parallel fetch per unique move URL (hundreds per game), no concurrency cap and no timeout; the 60s cache TTL in api.server.ts:8 means the fan-out repeats
findings.suggestion: Add AbortSignal.timeout to api(), cap concurrent fetches, and give immutable move data a longer TTL or fold it into the index build

findings.issue: PokeAPI response types are duplicated across route modules (Move in pokemon.tsx and move.tsx; Species/Pokemon only in pokemon.tsx; TypeRecord in api.server.ts), so an API shape change ripples through every route
findings.suggestion: Centralize all API response shapes in lib/api.server.ts (or a lib/pokeapi-types.ts) so the data module owns the boundary

findings.issue: Hand-rolled pre-hydration compensation (refs + activeElement checks + mount-time navigate), duplicated in pokemon.tsx:206-213
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared hook (or drive the search input from useSearchParams) instead of maintaining two copies of subtle hydration logic

findings.issue: fetch() has no AbortSignal/timeout, so a hung PokeAPI request hangs page rendering indefinitely
findings.suggestion: fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) }) and map timeouts to a 503-style error

findings.issue: isbot and @react-router/node are declared as direct dependencies but never imported; @react-router/dev and @react-router/express provide them transitively
findings.suggestion: Drop both from dependencies unless a custom entry.server (which would need isbot) is added

findings.issue: Splat route renders null and exists only to convert matches into 404 throws; the framework already routes unmatched URLs to the root ErrorBoundary with a 404
findings.suggestion: Either delete the route and let the built-in 404 flow reach the root boundary, or give it a real component instead of returning null

findings.issue: spriteUrl hard-codes the /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png pattern rather than using the sprite URLs the API returns
findings.suggestion: Keep the derivation (species-level cards would need a per-species fetch otherwise) but comment the spec dependency so a media-layout change is caught

summary: This app is squarely on the framework's current generation — React Router 8.5 with the React-19 <title> convention, typed route props, and data()-thrown 404s — and its dependency set is lean and modern. Data access is cleanly isolated behind one server-only module, so framework or API upgrades would touch very few files. The remaining age-well risks are duplicated PokeAPI type definitions, copy-pasted hydration compensation, and the absence of production error reporting or timeouts on upstream fetches.
